To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the two methods used to study the distribution of harbour porpoise in the Western Baltic Sea, satellite tracking and acoustic monitoring, showed a significant linear correlation.

1) the distribution patterns derived from satellite telemetry and passive acoustic monitoring were comparable; 2) the distribution patterns were similar for summer and autumn; 3) the distribution patterns showed a strong decline in harbour porpoise occurrence in the western part of the study area.

we have developed a method for comparing two very different methods for describing the relative distribution pattern of harbour porpoise, which showed that they are comparable in a low density environment.

the use of two methods to assess the distribution of harbour porpoise.

the MaxEnt model was able to predict the distribution patterns of porpoises with high accuracy.

both methods are useful and complementary in describing the relative distribution pattern in this area.

satellite telemetry and passive acoustic monitoring can provide similar results for the distribution of a population of cetaceans.
the two methods can be considered to be complementary and that the combination of the two methods can provide a more complete picture of porpoise distribution.

both MaxEnt models and C-PODs can be used as tools to monitor harbour porpoise distribution patterns in the western Baltic.
